observations:
Torah LM2/13 contains two explicit bechina statements that map cleanly to the two packages already proposed (Package 1: רְדִיפָה וְקֵרוּב לַה'; Package 2: הַשֵּׁם בְּכָל מָקוֹם). There is no independent domain of 3+ bechina-connected concepts in the source text beyond what is captured in those two packages.

The Torah is structurally complete as two packages:
- Package 2 (omnipresence) provides the ontological foundation
- Package 1 (persecution-flight-closeness) is the teaching that flows from that foundation

The relationship between the two packages is eitza (causal): Hashem's omnipresence [Package 2] → enables → the dynamic that every flight is a flight toward Hashem [Package 1]. This is cause-and-effect, not shared nature, so the two packages remain distinct.

There is no third domain. The Rebbe does not introduce any additional conceptual cluster — no evil domain, no structural/neutral domain, no additional good domain. The teaching is deliberately concentrated: one paradox, one proof, one Psalm verse, one Midrash. Adding a third package would require inventing connections not present in the text.

The only candidates for a third package might be: (1) the אֲבִיהֶם שֶׁבַּשָּׁמַיִם (Father in Heaven) concept, but this is used as a descriptive epithet for the destination of the drawing-near rather than a bechina-linked independent concept; (2) Israel/יִשְׂרָאֵל as the people being pursued, but the Torah treats them as the subject of the dynamic rather than a bechina concept in their own right. Neither meets the threshold of 3+ bechina-connected concepts forming an independent domain.
